stem: What is the width of the paper, in yards?
stimulus: A printmaker orders a roll of heavyweight paper for pulling large woodcut prints. The roll is 54 inches wide.
explanation: This question gives you a measurement in one unit and asks for it in another. There is no rate and no story to model. You need the standard factor 1 yard = 36 inches (3 feet per yard × 12 inches per foot). Write the conversion fraction with inches on the bottom so that inches cancel: $54 \text{ in} \times \dfrac{1 \text{ yd}}{36 \text{ in}} = \dfrac{54}{36} \text{ yd} = 1.5 \text{ yd}$. Check the direction: a yard is bigger than an inch, so the number of yards has to be smaller than 54. It is. If you prefer to chain through feet, do $54 \text{ in} \times \dfrac{1 \text{ ft}}{12 \text{ in}} \times \dfrac{1 \text{ yd}}{3 \text{ ft}} = 1.5 \text{ yd}$. Don't stop after the first factor.

common_errors.why: Multiplied 54 by 36 instead of dividing. That converts the wrong way and makes the yard count larger than the inch count.
Divided 54 by 12 to get feet and stopped there, without the second factor that converts feet to yards.
Used the wrong standard factor from memory, 3 inches per yard (mixing it up with 3 feet per yard), and computed 54 ÷ 3.
Used 12 inches per yard instead of 36 and computed 54 ÷ 12. This gives the same value as stopping at feet.

stem: How many gallons of water does the tank hold when it is full?
stimulus: A hydrologist stores groundwater samples in a holding tank with a volume of 77 cubic feet. One gallon is equal to 231 cubic inches.
explanation: This is a straight conversion from cubic feet to gallons. The question gives you the gallon in cubic inches, so you chain through cubic inches. First you need the cubic factor. Since 1 foot = 12 inches, 1 cubic foot = $12 \times 12 \times 12 = 1{,}728$ cubic inches, not 12. Then set up the chain so that each unwanted unit cancels: $77 \text{ ft}^3 \times \dfrac{1{,}728 \text{ in}^3}{1 \text{ ft}^3} \times \dfrac{1 \text{ gal}}{231 \text{ in}^3}$. Simplify before you multiply: $\dfrac{77}{231} = \dfrac{1}{3}$, so the result is $\dfrac{1{,}728}{3} = 576$ gallons. Check the direction: a gallon is smaller than a cubic foot, so the number of gallons should be larger than 77. It is.

common_errors.why: Used the linear factor 12 inches per foot instead of the cubic factor 1,728 cubic inches per cubic foot: 77 × 12 ÷ 231 = 4.
Used the square factor 144 instead of the cubic factor 1,728: 77 × 144 ÷ 231 = 48.
Converted to cubic inches (77 × 1,728) and stopped there, without dividing by 231 to get gallons.
Flipped both conversion fractions, computing 77 × 231 ÷ 1,728 ≈ 10.29. That converts the wrong way at each step.
Divided 77 by 231 and forgot to multiply by the cubic-inch factor at all.

stem: A labour economist studying unpaid overtime found that one employee worked a total of 7,200 minutes of unrecorded overtime in a year. The economist reports overtime in standard workdays, where 1 workday is 8 hours. How many workdays is 7,200 minutes equivalent to?
explanation: Write the amount with its unit, then multiply by fractions equal to 1 so that each unit you don't want cancels. First change minutes to hours, which you know: $7{,}200 \text{ min} \times \frac{1 \text{ hr}}{60 \text{ min}} = 120 \text{ hr}$. Then change hours to workdays using the factor given: $120 \text{ hr} \times \frac{1 \text{ workday}}{8 \text{ hr}} = 15 \text{ workdays}$. As one chain, that is $7{,}200 \times \frac{1}{60} \times \frac{1}{8} = 15$. Check the direction: a workday is a much larger unit than a minute, so the number should get much smaller, and it does.

common_errors.why: You changed minutes to hours and stopped there, so you never used the 8-hour workday.
You got 120 hours correctly, then multiplied by 8 instead of dividing. That converts the wrong way, as if a workday were smaller than an hour.
You divided 7,200 by 8 straight away and skipped the minutes-to-hours step, so you treated minutes as if they were hours.
You used a 24-hour calendar day ($120 \div 24$) in place of the stated 8-hour workday.

stem: A printmaker carves an image into a rectangular linoleum block with an area of 2.25 square feet. What is the area of the block, in square inches?
explanation: There are 12 inches in 1 foot. Square units hold one unit in each of two directions, so you need the conversion factor twice: $2.25 \text{ ft}^2 \times \frac{12 \text{ in}}{1 \text{ ft}} \times \frac{12 \text{ in}}{1 \text{ ft}} = 2.25 \times 144 \text{ in}^2 = 324 \text{ in}^2$. Check that the units cancel: both factors of ft cancel against $\text{ft}^2$ and leave $\text{in}^2$. Check the direction: an inch is smaller than a foot, so the number should get bigger.

common_errors.why: You multiplied by 12 only once, so one ft is left uncancelled. You found $\text{in}\cdot\text{ft}$, not square inches.
You divided by 144 instead of multiplying, which converts the wrong way. Going to a smaller unit must give a larger number. (Truncated value of $2.25/144 = 0.015625$.)
You divided by 12 just once, so you made both mistakes: the conversion goes the wrong way and is missing its second factor.
You applied the square to the 2.25 and the 12 together, as if the area were $(2.25 \cdot 12)^2/9$ or $(1.5 \cdot 6)^2$. Writing out the cancelling factors avoids this slip.
